concerns.text: Wilcoxon rank‑sum tests are performed per tissue without adjusting for known confounders (age, sex, PMI, Time_of_Death). In an observational setting these covariates can bias gene‑wise comparisons, so a simple non‑parametric test may yield spurious DE results.

Correlation analysis pools all donors across all tissues, ignoring tissue‑specific expression patterns. This can confound gene‑trait associations because expression levels differ markedly by tissue; a stratified or mixed‑effects approach would be more appropriate.

concerns.location: Risks & Mitigations – Insufficient complete GTEx donors (< 100) (plan.md:~120-130)
concerns.text: The plan sets a minimum of 100 complete donors as a cutoff for ‘exploratory’ status but provides no formal power calculation. For logistic regression with ~15 gene predictors plus covariates, 100 samples is likely underpowered, risking unstable coefficient estimates and inflated Type I error.

Logistic regression includes tissue as a one‑hot covariate but does not address potential batch effects or residual confounding from unmeasured variables (e.g., medication, cause of death). No sensitivity analysis is described to assess robustness of the predictive model.

concerns.location: Phase 3 – Differential Expression (plan.md:~70-85) and Phase 4 – Correlation (plan.md:~90-105)
concerns.text: Benjamini‑Hochberg FDR correction is applied separately within each tissue (DE) and per trait (correlation). This does not control the overall false discovery rate across all tissues/traits, potentially inflating the family‑wise error rate.

concerns.location: Assumptions – Post‑mortem expression reflects metabolic state (plan.md:~150-160)
concerns.text: The construct validity of using GTEx post‑mortem TPM as a proxy for in‑vivo metabolic syndrome biology is not justified beyond adding PMI and Time_of_Death as covariates. Circadian phase at death is not modeled, which may obscure true gene‑expression relationships.
